scenes.narration: Let's go through normalisation. Three things: what it is for, what first normal form asks of a table, and why the whole thing matters when your data starts changing.

Normalisation is how you organise a table so the same fact is not written down twice. If a lecturer's office number appears against every one of their courses, then moving office means finding every row.
First normal form asks one thing: every cell holds a single value. No lists, no repeating columns. If you have a phone one and a phone two column, you are not in first normal form.
The one thing to keep: normalisation is not about saving space. It is about making sure there is exactly one place to change when something changes.
